items.text: We measured how recursive synthetic-data training affects held-out real-text prediction and generated-text diversity, reconstructing the language-model setting in Shumailov et al. [1].
Baselines: untouched pretrained OPT and the real-data fine-tuned model G0.
Synthetic chain: G1–G10 use model-generated training targets.
Model: facebook/opt-125m, approximately 125 million parameters [2].
Dataset: Salesforce/wikitext, wikitext-2-raw-v1; an English Wikipedia-derived corpus [3].
Choice and reproducibility: this affordable setting matches [1]; model and dataset revisions are pinned.
Packing: preserve source rows and line breaks, use OPT’s default special tokens, concatenate within each split, then form disjoint 64-token blocks.
Evaluation: tokenize splits independently and discard only each final incomplete block. Validation selects checkpoints; fixed test blocks measure the selected model.
Recursive protocol
G0 = fine-tune(original pretrained OPT, real training blocks)
Dg = 64-token continuations generated by G(g-1)
Gg = fine-tune(original pretrained OPT, Dg), for g = 1,...,10
Generation: the preceding model receives all 37,946 real training blocks as 64-token prompts and produces exactly 64 new tokens per prompt.
Training targets: use continuation token IDs only; every new model starts from original pretrained OPT.
Replication limit: the authors’ precise per-generation initialization remains unresolved (Section 4).
Execution and reproducibility
Execution: 9.02 hours on RTX 2000 Ada; about $2.23 account debit through the 21 October check. Retained storage continues to bill.
Recovery and checks: checkpoints, synthetic data, configurations and metrics were backed up. All ten handoffs were audited; full-run checkpoints were not independently re-evaluated.
Table 1. Week 1 training configuration. Settings are fixed across G0–G10 unless stated otherwise.

items.text: Equal data budget: each D1–D10 matches the packed real training token count. Packing discarded 58 training, 41 validation and 29 test tokens.
Training exposure: five epochs per model give 12,142,720 input-token positions / 11,952,990 targets. Across 11 runs, 131,482,890 targets were processed; repeated passes do not create new data.
Final measurement: G10 generates a 256-prompt probe only; no G11 is trained.
Metric definitions
Prediction: corpus perplexity = exp(total next-token NLL / scored targets). P95 is the 95th percentile of mean NLL over 4,494 real test blocks.
Diversity and repetition: distinct-n = unique / total within-continuation n-grams. Repeated 4-grams = excess occurrences / total occurrences, pooled across the probe.

Other measures: duplicate rate = 1 − unique / total complete continuations; entropy = −sum(p log p) for empirical token frequencies, in nats. Frozen-G0 NLL scores continuations without prompts; it is descriptive, not a stand-alone quality measure.
Fixed probe: the same first 256 training prompts yield 16,384 continuation tokens and 15,616 within-continuation 4-gram positions. Special tokens are retained.
Interpretation: this contiguous probe is not a random corpus sample. Loss/PPL are linked, as are distinct-n and repetition statistics.

Table 2. Token counts use the OPT tokenizer and include special tokens. The 64-token blocks are the experimental units. Each supplies 63 shifted next-token targets; prompts are not counted as synthetic training targets.

items.text: Figure 1. One-seed results. (a) Fixed real validation/test sets; pretrained baseline 115.43 is omitted for readability. (b-e) Fixed 256-prompt probe. (f) Same 4,494 test blocks and common bins. This distribution describes variation among blocks, not uncertainty across independent training runs.
Key findings
Perplexity: 115.43 before real-data fine-tuning → 33.88 at G0 → 62.49 at G1, then approximately 52–54. G10 remains 55.9% above G0.
Generated text: repetition rises by 10.2 percentage points overall; distinct-3 declines while distinct-2 increases (Table 3).
High-loss blocks: P95 NLL increases from 4.478 to 4.955. This describes the test set’s high-loss tail, not rare-token loss.
Trajectory: neither perplexity nor repetition must change monotonically.

items.text: Interpretation
Largest change: the initial real-to-synthetic transition produces the largest measured loss.
Possible plateau mechanism: a stable, biased distribution may emerge; pretrained initialization, real prompts and validation selection may constrain drift. This explanation is not established.
Different measurements: perplexity scores real next tokens given correct real prefixes; beam-generated text follows the model’s own outputs, so the trends can differ.
Limitations
Replication limits: one seed; differences in packing, precision and score aggregation; a different repetition penalty in released code; unresolved source-checkpoint orchestration.
Sampling limit: the probe contains the first 256 training blocks.
Supported finding: lasting loss relative to G0 and greater repetition overall. This does not establish factual accuracy, loss of rare events or complete collapse.
Sources: [1] Shumailov et al. (2024), Nature. [2] OPT-125M model card. [3] WikiText dataset card. Reproducibility: GitHub report and records.

items.text: We tested continued self-training: each cycle learns from text generated by its preceding selected checkpoint. The chain is labelled S0–S10.
Starting point: S0 is the exact saved real-data-trained checkpoint, verified by model-tensor and checkpoint-file hashes; it is imported rather than retrained.
Fixed setup: model/tokenizer and WikiText-2 raw revisions, packing and real evaluation arrays remain fixed. This is a defined continued-weight protocol, not an exact paper-replication claim.
Recursive protocol
S0 = saved real-data G0 from Week 1
D(k+1) = generate(Sk, fixed real training prompts)
S(k+1) = fine-tune(Sk, D(k+1)), k = 0,...,9
Generation: each selected model receives the same 37,946 real training blocks as 64-token prompts and generates exactly 64 new tokens per prompt.
Training: use continuation IDs only, excluding prompts. Initialize from the model that generated those targets; restart AdamW and the scheduler each cycle.
Execution and checks
Execution: 6.77 hours on RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell; about $3.99 observed account debit including retained storage, not an itemized compute invoice. GPU shutdown was verified.
Validation scope: all ten weight/data handoffs were checked and all 11 probe-diversity measurements recalculated. Bulk checkpoints were not downloaded or re-evaluated.
Table 5. Continued-training configuration. S0 is imported; each synthetic cycle carries the selected weights and restarts AdamW and the scheduler.

items.text: Equal token budget: each D1–D10 matches the packed real training pool.
Fixed evaluation: concatenate each split independently and discard its final incomplete block; validation/test arrays remain unchanged across all cycles.
Generated data: ten complete training datasets contain 24,285,440 tokens.
Training exposure: 10 × 5 epochs; 121,427,200 input-token exposures.
Final probe: S10 produces 256 measurement outputs; no full D11 or S11.
Metric definitions
Corpus perplexity: exp(total next-token NLL / scored targets). Each 64-token block supplies 63 targets: 247,086 validation and 283,122 test targets.
Passage statistics: P95 is the 95th percentile of mean test-block NLL. Passage-PPL mean/SD are distinct from corpus PPL and are not across-seed uncertainty.
Fixed output probe: 256 prompts, 16,384 continuation tokens and 15,616 within-continuation 4-gram positions.
Diversity: pool within-continuation n-grams without crossing boundaries; exact duplicates compare complete rows; entropy is empirical unigram entropy in nats.
Frozen reference: S0 scores each continuation alone over 63 targets, without the original prompt. This score is not KL divergence.
Table 6. Continued-training data budget. Each synthetic dataset matches the packed real training pool; each 64-token block supplies 63 prediction targets.

items.text: Interpretation and checkpoint selection
Observed pattern: fitting synthetic targets while real validation loss worsens is consistent with a synthetic/real-text mismatch.
Possible mechanism: repeated weight updates may accumulate that mismatch; this run does not establish the cause.
Selection: epoch 1 has the lowest real validation loss in every cycle; all five epochs still ran.
Inherited weights: S10 carries ten selected synthetic-training epochs after S0, rather than all fifty executed epochs.
Limitations
Limits: one seed, fixed real prompts and real-validation checkpoint selection. These results do not prove loss of rare events, factual accuracy or complete collapse.

Sources and reproducibility: Week 1 sources [1–3] remain applicable. Week 2 report, complete metric table, saved histories and consistency audit are linked below; private backups retain all 11 checkpoints and synthetic datasets.
Week 2 report and reproducibility records.

items.text: OPT-125M / WikiText-2. New reset run: 20261027T211852Z-full-reset-s0. Completed 28 October 2026; seed 42.
We reused the continued run’s exact S0, S1 and D2 to create an identical first synthetic-training step.
Common prefix: S0 is real-data-trained; S1 starts from S0 and learns from S0-generated D1. The S0/S1 evaluations are the same saved measurements.
Labels: B2–B10 are the previously reported S2–S10; A2–A10 are the new reset branch.
First difference: cycle 2 uses identical S1-generated D2 in both arms. A2 starts from S0; B2 starts from S1.
Later cycles: each arm generates its own next dataset, allowing weight history and synthetic content to diverge.
Reset definition: always initialize from real-trained S0; this differs from Week 1’s reset to untouched pretrained OPT.
Shared prefix and branch
Shared: S0 -> generate D1 -> train S0 on D1 -> S1 -> generate D2
Cycle 2: A2 = train(S0, D2); B2 = train(S1, D2)
Later: A(k+1) = train(S0, generate(Ak))
B(k+1) = train(Bk, generate(Bk))

Matched settings: fixed prompts/splits, 64 new tokens, five deterministic beams, repetition penalty 1.0; five epochs, fresh AdamW/scheduler, LR 2e-5 with epoch cosine towards 1e-6, batch 128, BF16, seed 42.
Matched environment: recorded GPU class, driver, Python and primary libraries agree—RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell and PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128.
Data budget and execution
Equal datasets: continuation IDs only; 2,428,544 tokens per training dataset, matching the real pool.
New training: A2–A10 execute 45 epochs / 109,284,480 input-token exposures.
New generation: import D2, generate eight full datasets DA3–DA10 (19,428,352 tokens), then a 16,384-token A10 probe. Shared work is not rerun or charged again.
Execution: 5.62 hours; shutdown verified; about $3.36 account debit including storage, not an itemized compute invoice.
Checks: checkpoint hashes, nine handoffs, fixed splits/environments and all 20 distinct model probes. Bulk checkpoints were not re-evaluated.
Table 9. Data sizes shared by the reset and continued arms. Prompt and training-token budgets match; the real evaluation arrays remain fixed.

items.text: Figure 3. The grey prefix is the single shared S0/S1 measurement pair. Purple resets to real-trained S0 (A); orange continues the previous weights (B). Curves first diverge at cycle 2. Real-test scoring and the first 256 output prompts are fixed. One seeded pair; no across-run error bars.
Key findings
Identical first step: both arms share test PPL 33.89 → 48.38.
Cycle 2: A2 = 40.95 versus B2 = 42.97, 4.72% lower.
Later trajectory: reset stays at 40.00–42.13 from A3 onward; continued rises from 42.72 at B3 to 55.56 at B10. A10 = 42.10, 24.22% below B10 but 24.25% above S0.
Reset output concentration: distinct-2 falls from 42.22% at A2 to 31.05% at A10; repeated 4-grams rise from 40.95% to 57.66%; entropy falls by 1.123 nats.
Interpretation: better real-text prediction does not imply preservation of every aspect of generated-text diversity.

items.text: Figure 4. A: final real-test block-loss distributions; reset has lower loss on 4,340/4,494 matched blocks (96.57%), a descriptive paired result. B: real-validation loss across five epochs for cycles 2/10; stars mark the selected checkpoint. These are within-cycle measurements, not independent replicates.
Real-text prediction
Final real-test loss: 3.740 for A10 versus 4.017 for B10; difference 0.277 nats per target. P95 block NLL is 4.629 versus 4.998.
Coverage: reset improves most fixed test blocks, beyond a few extreme passages. These blocks are not independent training replicates.
Checkpoint selection and interpretation
Selection: epoch 1 is chosen in every new reset stage; all 45 new epochs still ran.
Reset inheritance: A10 starts from S0 and retains its own selected synthetic epoch, not earlier A-model updates. Its data still carry the recursive history.
Continued inheritance: B10 carries ten selected synthetic epochs after S0. Selection compares epochs 1–5; unmodified S0 is not a candidate.
Possible mechanism: fixed-S0 initialization may limit accumulated weight drift while deterministic feedback concentrates synthetic text; this is an interpretation, not an isolated mechanism test.
Frozen-S0 score: A10’s 2.127 versus B10’s 2.343 means more predictable continuations under S0, not greater factuality or prompt relevance; it is not KL divergence.
Conclusion: lower perplexity alone is insufficient evidence that collapse has been prevented.
Limitations

Design: one seed and a historical continued arm. Matched artifacts, data and recorded environment remove the first-cycle mismatch, but do not ensure cross-launch bitwise equality or statistical significance.
Protocol scope: real prompts at every cycle and real-validation checkpoint selection.
Measurement limits: a fixed 256-prompt probe; tail block loss does not identify rare-token loss. This compares two defined protocols, not every condition of the original paper.

Reproducibility: 1,392 metadata files (41.51 MB) were checksum-verified; nine new probe arrays added 590,976 bytes. The comparison audit checks 170 statistics files, all 95 executed historical/new epoch records and the exact common prefix. The complete per-cycle CSV, all 256 saved outputs per model, figures and audit are retained with pinned private backup revisions.
Shared-start report, complete statistics and reproducible analysis.
